questions.question: About what percentage of the Earth's surface is covered by water?
questions.explanation: Earth's surface is about 71% water, 29% land.

questions.question: About what percentage of the Earth's surface is land?
How many continents are there?
questions.explanation: Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe, Australia.

questions.question: Which is the LARGEST continent?
questions.explanation: Asia is by far the biggest, ~30% of all land.

questions.question: Which is the SMALLEST continent?
questions.explanation: Australia is the smallest of the seven.

questions.question: Which is the SECOND-largest continent?
In the order of size (largest to smallest), which is THIRD?
questions.explanation: Asia, Africa, NORTH AMERICA, South America, Antarctica, Europe, Australia.

questions.question: How many oceans are there in modern geography?
Which is the LARGEST ocean?
questions.explanation: Pacific covers nearly one-third of Earth's surface.

questions.question: Which is the SMALLEST ocean?
questions.explanation: Arctic is the smallest, surrounding the North Pole.

questions.question: Which ocean lies between the Americas and Europe / Africa?
Which ocean lies SOUTH of India?
questions.explanation: India sits at the northern edge of the Indian Ocean.

questions.question: Which ocean surrounds Antarctica?
The Sahara desert is in which continent?
The Amazon rainforest is in which continent?
questions.explanation: World's largest rainforest, mostly in Brazil.

questions.question: The Himalayan mountain range is in which continent?
Kangaroos and koalas are native animals of which continent?
The Andes mountain range is in which continent?
questions.explanation: Longest mountain range; runs along the western edge of South America.

questions.question: The Nile river is in which continent?
questions.explanation: One of the longest rivers in the world; in north-east Africa.

questions.question: The South Pole lies in which continent?
The Alps mountains are mainly in which continent?
Which oceans border North America?
Which oceans border Africa?
questions.explanation: Africa is bordered by Atlantic on the west and Indian on the east.

questions.question: Which ocean is bordered by Asia, Africa, Australia AND Antarctica (Southern Ocean)?
India is located in which continent?
Which ocean is to the SOUTH of India?
questions.explanation: India sits at the northern edge of the Indian Ocean.

questions.question: Which is NOT a neighbour of India?
The country directly to the SOUTH of India (across the sea) is:
The arm of the Indian Ocean to the EAST of India is called:
questions.explanation: Bay of Bengal lies east of India.

questions.question: The arm of the Indian Ocean to the WEST of India is called:
questions.explanation: Arabian Sea lies west of India.

questions.question: Which line of latitude passes through the middle of India?
questions.explanation: Tropic of Cancer (23½° N) passes through central India.

questions.question: Because the Tropic of Cancer passes through India, most of India lies in which heat zone?
questions.explanation: Torrid Zone (between the two tropics) — hot.

questions.question: Compare Asia and Australia by SIZE.
questions.explanation: Asia is the largest continent; Australia is the smallest.

questions.question: Which is the COLDEST continent?
Which continent has NO permanent human population (only research stations)?
questions.explanation: Researchers visit but no one lives permanently.

questions.question: Which continent is sometimes also called Oceania?
questions.explanation: Australia + the Pacific islands together are sometimes called Oceania.

questions.question: Which ocean is the DEEPEST?
questions.explanation: Pacific is the deepest; the Mariana Trench is in the Pacific.

questions.question: The Atacama desert is in which continent?
questions.explanation: Atacama (in Chile) is the world's driest non-polar desert.

questions.question: The Great Lakes are between which two countries?
questions.explanation: Great Lakes lie on the border in North America.

questions.question: Which ocean is to the EAST of Asia?
questions.explanation: Pacific borders Asia on the east (Japan, China's east coast, etc.).

questions.question: Which continent has the LARGEST population?
questions.explanation: About 60% of the world's people live in Asia.

questions.question: Most of the Earth's surface is covered by water.
Antarctica is the smallest continent.
questions.explanation: Australia is the smallest; Antarctica is fifth-largest.

questions.question: The Indian Ocean is the largest ocean.
questions.explanation: Pacific is the largest; Indian is third.

questions.question: All five oceans are connected to one another.
The Sahara is the world's largest hot desert.
India is part of the continent of Africa.
The Bay of Bengal lies to the east of India.
The largest continent on Earth is ____.
The smallest continent is ____.
The largest ocean is the ____.
The smallest ocean is the ____.
India is in the continent of ____.
The Tropic of Cancer (23½° N) passes through the country of ____.
Name all seven continents in order from largest to smallest.
questions.answer: 1. Asia, 2. Africa, 3. North America, 4. South America, 5. Antarctica, 6. Europe, 7. Australia.

questions.question: Name all five oceans and roughly where each lies.
questions.answer: 1. Pacific — between Asia/Australia and the Americas (largest). 2. Atlantic — between the Americas and Europe/Africa. 3. Indian — south of Asia, west of Australia, east of Africa. 4. Southern (Antarctic) — surrounds Antarctica. 5. Arctic — surrounds the North Pole (smallest).

questions.question: Match each feature to its continent: Sahara, Amazon, Himalayas, Great Barrier Reef.
questions.answer: Sahara → Africa. Amazon → South America. Himalayas → Asia. Great Barrier Reef → Australia.

questions.question: Name the oceans bordering each: (a) Africa, (b) Australia, (c) North America.
questions.answer: (a) Africa: Atlantic (west) + Indian (east). (b) Australia: Indian (west) + Pacific (east) + Southern (south). (c) North America: Pacific (west) + Atlantic (east) + Arctic (north).

questions.question: Name three countries that share a land border with India.
questions.answer: Any three of: Pakistan (west), China, Nepal, Bhutan (north), Myanmar, Bangladesh (east).

questions.question: Why does most of India experience hot summers? Use the heat-zone idea.
questions.answer: The Tropic of Cancer (23½° N) passes through the middle of India. The area between the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn is the TORRID Zone — the hottest part of the Earth, where the sun is overhead twice a year. Most of India lies in or just north of the Torrid Zone, so it experiences strong, direct sunlight and hot summers.
questions.explanation: Connects Tropic of Cancer to climate.

questions.question: Compare Antarctica and Australia in size, climate, and population.
questions.answer: Size: Antarctica is larger (5th-largest) than Australia (smallest). Climate: Antarctica is the COLDEST continent (covered in ice); Australia is mostly hot and dry. Population: Antarctica has NO permanent population (only research stations); Australia has tens of millions of people. So they are opposite in many ways despite both being in the southern hemisphere.

questions.question: Pick TWO continents you know best. For each, write 3-4 sentences describing its location, key feature, climate, and one country found there.
questions.answer: Sample (Asia + Africa). ASIA — Located on the eastern side of the Eastern Hemisphere; the largest continent. Key features include the Himalayas (highest mountains in the world) and the Gobi desert. Climates vary from polar (Siberia) to tropical (India, Indonesia). India is one of the major countries here, with about 1.4 billion people. AFRICA — Located south of Europe and west of Asia, in the centre of the Eastern Hemisphere. Key features include the Sahara desert (the world's largest hot desert) and the Nile River (one of the longest rivers in the world). Climate is mostly hot, with rainforests in the central belt and deserts in the north and south. Egypt is a major country, with the famous pyramids and a long history along the Nile.
questions.explanation: Open-ended; rubric: location + feature + climate + country, for two continents.

questions.question: Why is India's location strategically and culturally important? Discuss in 5-6 sentences.
questions.answer: India sits at the meeting point of three continents (via the Indian Ocean, which links it to Africa, the Middle East, Southeast Asia and onwards to Europe). The Indian Ocean has been a corridor for trade and cultural exchange for thousands of years — spices, textiles, ideas and religions have travelled in and out of India by sea. India's neighbours include China and Pakistan (large countries with long histories of interaction with India) and the smaller Himalayan kingdoms (Nepal, Bhutan). The Tropic of Cancer passes through India, giving most of the country a warm climate suitable for year-round farming and a great variety of crops. Strategically, India lies along the major sea-route between Europe / Africa and East Asia. Culturally, it has absorbed influences from many directions and shared its own influences widely.
questions.explanation: Connects geography to history and trade.

questions.question: Suppose you could visit any one continent. Which would you choose and why? Compare it (briefly) with two others to justify your choice. Use at least one feature, one climate fact, and one cultural / wildlife fact.
questions.answer: Sample answer: 'I would choose AFRICA because of its incredible wildlife (lions, elephants, giraffes — found in the savannah of countries like Kenya and Tanzania). The climate ranges from rainforest in the equatorial belt to desert (Sahara) in the north — a huge variety in one continent. Compared with ASIA, Africa has fewer people per square kilometre and more open wild spaces. Compared with EUROPE, Africa is much bigger and has older human-history sites (the Egyptian pyramids, very early human fossils). The combination of wildlife, climate range, and ancient history makes Africa my first choice.' (Open-ended; rubric: chosen continent + 2 comparisons + a feature + a climate fact + a culture / wildlife fact.)
